name: Eleazar (son of Aaron)
title: Israel's third high priest
summary: Eleazar was the third son of Aaron and succeeded his father as high priest in Israel. He served faithfully through the wilderness journey and into the Promised Land, playing a central role in distributing Canaan among the tribes. His descendants continued the priesthood for generations.

keyEvents.title: Consecrated for priestly service
keyEvents.description: Eleazar was consecrated along with his father Aaron and his brothers for priestly service at the tabernacle on Sinai.

keyEvents.title: Took over after the death of his brothers
keyEvents.description: When Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, Eleazar and Ithamar were given expanded responsibility in the priestly service.

keyEvents.title: Leader of the Levites
keyEvents.description: Eleazar was appointed as the chief leader of the Levites and had oversight over those who served in the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: Aaron's robe on Mount Hor
keyEvents.description: When Aaron was to die on Mount Hor, Moses took the priestly garments from Aaron and clothed Eleazar with them, and Eleazar became high priest.

keyEvents.title: Distribution of the land of Canaan
keyEvents.description: Together with Joshua, Eleazar led the distribution of the promised land among the tribes of Israel by casting lots.

keyEvents.title: Death and burial
keyEvents.description: Eleazar died and was buried on a hill in the hill country of Ephraim that belonged to his son Phinehas.
